entries.title: Research a prospect and draft outreach
entries.description: For a made-up regional freight company, Cowork researched what businesses like it are facing right now, worked out what its revenue operations lead likely cares about, and wrote a brief and a first email.

draft.label: The first email, ready to edit and send
draft.text:
Subject: Connecting freight growth to fulfillment economics

Hi there,

I noticed Fernhill is growing its e-commerce fulfillment line alongside its Midwest trucking and warehousing business. That kind of expansion can make it harder to connect what sales promises with the true account economics and day-to-day service performance, especially as freight capacity and costs shift.

I’d be interested in how you’re thinking about visibility across the customer journey, from quote and operating cost through fulfillment and delivery, and where RevOps is focusing first. Would a 20-minute conversation next week be useful?

Best,
[Your name]

blocks.text: The opening thesis: freight is getting less forgiving just as fulfillment adds complexity, so the useful conversation is how Fernhill grows the new line without losing sight of account margin, service quality or capacity.
What is happening in the industry

items: Capacity, not a demand boom, is tightening truckload: tonnage flat year over year, spot rates up in October with diesel behind much of it.
Fulfillment is growing selectively: value-added warehousing up an estimated 4.4% in 2025, with automation bought only where it pays back.
Logistics surveys put freight-cost control, shipment visibility and practical AI first, with data quality the main barrier.

entries.title: Turn a bank statement into a spreadsheet
entries.description: Cowork made a sample one-month bank statement, turned it into a workbook with one transaction per row and a running balance, and checked that the totals match.

blocks.text: 22 transactions, one per row with date, description, money in, money out and running balance. Every running balance matches the statement, so nothing was left to reconcile. The bank, account holder and transactions are made up.

entries.title: Make a study guide from course material
entries.description: Cowork wrote sample lecture notes on contract law, then a study guide from them: key concepts, definitions in the notes’ exact words, a glossary and a 10-question quiz with answers.

blocks.text: Definitions, word for word from the notes

items: Offer: a communication showing willingness to make a bargain on sufficiently definite terms, such that the recipient can accept and conclude the bargain.
Consideration: a bargained-for exchange in which each side gives, promises, or undertakes something the law treats as value.
Breach: a failure, without legal excuse, to perform a contractual duty when performance is due.
